taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 21 p. 453, 454 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Psilostrophe cooperi: shrubs or subshrubs, (15-)25-30(-50+) cm.

traits.height_max_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 21 p. 453, 454 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Psilostrophe cooperi: (15-)25-30(-50+) cm; the 50 cm is taken as its greatest.

traits.life_span.note: Kearney and Peebles, Flowering Plants and Ferns of Arizona (1942) p. 969, Psilostrophe cooperi: plant definitely shrubby (key to species), flowering throughout the year.

traits.woodiness.note: Flora of North America vol. 21 p. 453, 454 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Psilostrophe cooperi: shrubs or subshrubs; Kearney and Peebles (1942 p. 969): plant definitely shrubby. Drawn semi-woody, a subshrub's woody base.

traits.rosette.note: Leaves along the branches, with no basal rosette, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 261208822, 261806410, 180482349, 397176318, 141908100, 115520642, 214501789, 216012053): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Flora of North America vol. 21 p. 415, 416 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Psilostrophe (genus): leaves basal and cauline or all cauline; alternate.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: leaves 1.5 cm to 5 cm long, as in the photos.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: leaves 1.5 mm to 4 mm wide, linear, as in the photos.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Kearney and Peebles, Flowering Plants and Ferns of Arizona (1942) p. 969, Psilostrophe cooperi: leaves linear or narrowly linear-lanceolate, entire (key to species).

traits.leaf_margin.note: Kearney and Peebles, Flowering Plants and Ferns of Arizona (1942) p. 969, Psilostrophe cooperi: leaves linear or narrowly linear-lanceolate, entire (key to species).

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Flora of North America vol. 21 p. 415, 416 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Psilostrophe (genus): faces densely to sparsely arachno-villous or more or less strigillose; the species' stems pannose, white.

traits.leaf_division.note: Flora of North America vol. 21 p. 415, 416 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Psilostrophe (genus): blades spatulate to oblanceolate or linear, margins usually entire.

traits.inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 21 p. 453, 454 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Psilostrophe cooperi: heads borne singly; Kearney and Peebles (1942 p. 969): heads mostly solitary at the tips of the branches, slender-peduncled.

traits.peduncle_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 21 p. 453, 454 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Psilostrophe cooperi: peduncles 35-60(-80+) mm.

traits.capitulum_kind.note: Flora of North America vol. 21 p. 415, 416 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Psilostrophe (genus): heads radiate.

traits.involucre_height_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 21 p. 453, 454 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Psilostrophe cooperi: involucres 6-8 mm.

traits.involucre_diameter_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: involucres 5 mm to 7 mm across, at the top of the 2-7 mm FNA gives the genus (vol. 21 p. 415).

traits.phyllaries.note: Flora of North America vol. 21 p. 415, 416 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Psilostrophe (genus): phyllaries persistent, 5-12 in 1-2 series.

traits.phyllary_series.note: Flora of North America vol. 21 p. 415, 416 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Psilostrophe (genus): phyllaries 5-12 in 1-2 series.

traits.ray_florets.note: Flora of North America vol. 21 p. 453, 454 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Psilostrophe cooperi: rays 3-6; the photos show 3 to 5.

traits.ray_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 21 p. 453, 454 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Psilostrophe cooperi: ray laminae (8-)12-20 mm, spreading to reflexed in fruit.

traits.ray_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: ray laminae 7 mm to 12 mm wide, broad and fan-shaped, about two thirds as wide as long in the photos.

traits.ray_apex.note: Each ray broad and ending in three teeth, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 261208822, 261806410, 180482349, 397176318, 141908100, 115520642, 214501789, 216012053): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.ray_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 21 p. 415, 416 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Psilostrophe (genus): ray corollas yellow to orange, marcescent; bright lemon yellow in the photos, drying papery and pale; sRGB by eye.

traits.disc_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 21 p. 415, 416 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Psilostrophe (genus): disc corollas yellow to orange; sRGB by eye from the photos.

traits.disc_florets.note: Flora of North America vol. 21 p. 453, 454 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Psilostrophe cooperi: disc florets (6-)10-17(-25).

traits.pappus.note: Flora of North America vol. 21 p. 453, 454 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Psilostrophe cooperi: pappi of 4-6 oblong to more or less lanceolate scales 2-2.5 mm.

traits.fruit_type.note: Flora of North America vol. 21 p. 453, 454 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Psilostrophe cooperi: cypselae usually glabrous, sometimes gland-dotted.

traits.flowering_months.note: Flora of North America vol. 21 p. 453, 454 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Psilostrophe cooperi: flowering (Feb-)Apr-Jun(-Dec); Kearney and Peebles (1942 p. 969): flowering throughout the year. The main spring flush is drawn.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: cypselae ripe May to July, after the spring flowering, the papery rays still on the heads.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a low, rounded mound of white-woolly stems and sparse narrow grey-green leaves, covered in spring with bright yellow heads of three to five broad, three-toothed rays that dry papery on the plant. Colours set by eye were written as screen (sRGB) shades; they are read as the linear light a colour field holds, and bark and foliage follow the stated colour traits by rule (2026-10-19).

generator.params.note: Set by hand for paperflower from its sources and the photos the traits cite; the rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.27 m tall at 15 years in the open, within its sources' typical 25-30 cm, as grown (the drawn bush is 0.15-0.17 m at 5 years, still filling out). Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added for the Saguaro desert scene (west bajada of Saguaro National Park's Tucson Mountain District, about 750 m), batch s1b (2026-10-19): sizes and forms from FEIS, Kearney and Peebles, Hitchcock and Flora of North America, counts and colours from photos.
